author: massicomar
title: Convex Hull
summary:
Given a set of 2D points in a plane, you must compute the smallest convex polygon that encloses all the given points. Input

Input contains several test cases. Each test case begins with an integer $n$ ($1 \leq n \leq 10000$). Then follow a list of $n$ points, one per line, each of the form $x\ y$. Coordinates are integer with absolute value bounded by 10000. The input is terminated by a case beginning with 0.

Warning! This problem has a slighly largish input file

Output

For each test case, output a polygon giving the smallest convex polygon that encloses all of the input points, in the same format as the input. This polygon should not contain any colinear edges, and should be given in counterclockwise order.
explanation: Monotone chain hull. This judge wants collinear points removed.
traps: Collinear points: this problem excludes them, CSES 2195 includes them.
